evidence.claim: Sysco is a global leader in selling, marketing, and distributing food and related products to food-away-from-home customers and reported more than $81 billion of fiscal 2025 sales.

Reborn Coffee announced a distribution partnership with Sysco intended to support national franchise expansion, fulfillment reliability, quality assurance resources, food safety protocols, local sourcing support, and operational tools.
evidence.source_title: Reborn Coffee Announces Strategic Distribution Partnership with Sysco to Support National Franchise Expansion

evidence.claim: National DCP describes itself as a $3 billion supply-chain management company serving Dunkin' franchisees, supporting over 10,000 Dunkin' quick-service restaurants in the U.S. and distributing products to more than 40 countries.

Performance Food Group markets and distributes food and food-related products across North America from distribution centers to customer locations in the food-away-from-home industry, including chain customers and recognizable family and casual dining restaurant chains.

Performance Food Group investor materials describe more than 150 locations and delivery of products to 300,000-plus locations including independent and chain restaurants, office coffee service distributors, theaters, and convenience stores.

memory_update.text: SYY should remain the reference anchor for restaurant and franchise supply-chain orchestration, but it is not the main underfollowed discovery target.
PFGC is a strong public-market mapping for national-chain and broadline foodservice distribution; include in later layers if the pass allows large-cap pure-play infrastructure names.

CHEF is an underfollowed mid-cap specialty-distribution angle; future layers should verify whether it has meaningful multi-unit restaurant or franchise-system exposure rather than mostly independent chef-driven customers.

HFFG is a speculative micro-cap niche-distributor exception; retain only if later evidence identifies scaled Asian restaurant, QSR, franchise, or multi-unit customer relationships and governance risks are acceptable for research tracking.

NDCP remains the private reference model for how franchise co-ops can manage sourcing, cost-of-goods reduction, product availability, limited-time-offer forecasting, and assured supply for a large coffee/QSR system.

Need a focused follow-up search for public niche software, EDI, food-safety, QA, demand-forecasting, and purchasing-platform vendors embedded in restaurant franchise supply chains; current pass found mostly distributor mappings.

node: Franchise procurement, sourcing, and supply-chain orchestration
summary: Layer 1B expands the public universe around outsourced restaurant/franchise supply-chain orchestration. The reference lane confirms that broadline foodservice distributors can function as hidden infrastructure for restaurant standardization, procurement, quality assurance, and franchise readiness. The underfollowed lane points to more obscure specialty or niche distributors where restaurant demand, fragmented customer bases, supplier relationships, and distribution density may create second-order exposure. No buy/sell recommendation is made.
